edit.statement: 'Member of' is functional: a person is a member of (a delegate to) at most one assembly.
edit.subject: member_of
edit.original: 'Member of' is not functional: a person can be a member of several assemblies.
edit.scope: Membership of persons in assemblies, councils and societies; which bodies exist is untouched.

direct.prompt: May one person be a member of two explicitly different assemblies?

paraphrase.prompt: Does the rule for 'member of' allow a single person to belong to two distinct bodies?

cross_lingual.prompt: 同一个人可以是两个明确不同的议会的成员吗？
¿Puede una misma persona ser miembro de dos asambleas explícitamente distintas?

derived.prompt: Proposed facts: George Washington was a delegate to the First Continental Congress; George Washington was a delegate to the Constitutional Convention; the two assemblies are explicitly different. Is this configuration consistent or inconsistent with the rule?
bridge: George Washington was a delegate to the First Continental Congress.
George Washington was a delegate to the Constitutional Convention.
the two assemblies are explicitly different.

notes: Locality reference is the logical answer; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer. Washington, Churchill (FRS 1941) and Franklin did belong to both bodies named, so the real configurations are true and become inconsistent only under the edited rule.
